blocks.prompt: 4. Determine the total worth of a yearly Rs. 5000 investment after 20 years if the interest rate is 5% compounded annually.
blocks.explanation:
A new Rs. 5000 is invested every year; each deposit grows at 5% compound interest for a different number of years.
The final values of the deposits form a G.P., so the total worth is the SUM of a G.P.
Plan: take each deposit at the start of a year (this is what the key's answer uses), list what each grows to, add with \(S_n = \frac{a_1(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}\).
steps:
Given: Rs. 5000 invested at the start of every year for 20 years, 5% compounded annually.
To find: the total worth \(W\) after 20 years.
Method: Each deposit's final value is \(5000(1.05)^k\); these form a G.P., so use \(S_n = \frac{a_1(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}\) (as \(r > 1\)).

Find what each deposit grows to
\[\text{1st}: 5000(1.05)^{20}\]
\[\text{2nd}: 5000(1.05)^{19}\]
\[\ldots\]
\[\text{20th}: 5000(1.05)^{1}\]
Why: A deposit made at the start of year \(k\) stays invested \(21 - k\) years, gaining one factor 1.05 per year.

Write the total as a G.P.
\[W = 5000(1.05) + 5000(1.05)^2\]
\[+ \ldots + 5000(1.05)^{20}\]
\[a_1 = 5250,\ r = 1.05,\ n = 20\]
Why: Written from smallest to largest, each term is 1.05 times the one before; \(5000 \times 1.05 = 5250\).

Work out \((1.05)^{20}\)
\[(1.05)^5 = 1.2762815625\]
\[(1.05)^{10} \approx 1.62889463\]
\[(1.05)^{20} \approx 2.65329771\]
Why: Start from \((1.05)^5\) (as in Question 3), square to get the 10th power, square again for the 20th.

Find the total worth
\[W \approx 105000 \times 1.65329771\]
\[\approx 173596.26\]
Why: Subtract 1, multiply by 105000.
